newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends limit-up on LME gains.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends limit-up on LME gains.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended sharply up on Monday, with most contracts closing limit-up in active trading, thanks to sharp rises last Friday on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active December 1996 contract ended at limit-up of 21,190 yuan ($2,551) per tonne, rising 630 yuan. It opened at an intra-day low of 21,180.

September rose 300 to 21,500 yuan, October 520 to 21,400, November 610 to 21,230, the January 1997 contract 630 to 21,180, February 620 to 21,210 and March 610 to 21,010. April did not trade. May rose 10 to 21,010.
Combined volume rose sharply to 40,150 tonnes from 15,615.
Most contracts opened sharply up, hitting limit-up and staying at that level for the whole session.
Traders said that last Friday's breakthrough of a key $1,970 resistance level on the LME boosted confidence of long-position holders and copper is likely to rise further in the next few days.

"Market sentiment has clearly improved," one trader said. "All later-maturing contracts breached the key 21,000-yuan resistance level in heavy volume, which indicated copper will rise further in the short term."
"Copper's rebound is due to positive technical charts and a recent strike by Chilean copper workers," a second traders said.
"Expectations of increasing demand for spot copper also helped copper rise," he added.
Analysts expect copper to rise further in the short term.
Aluminium ended up. September rose 10 to 14,400 yuan, October 180 to 14,480 and November 200 to 14,500.
Combined volume rose to 1,710 tonnes from 410.
